GM from the mass 0.05810339 Jupiter masses (Burt et al. 2020, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2020AJ....160..153B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..153B/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. sources.period: Kokori et al. 2023 (2023ApJS..265....4K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KOKORI_ET_AL__2023): P 1.392975 d
sources.shape: Burt et al. 2020 (2020AJ....160..153B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BURT_ET_AL__2020): a/R* 6.73; Burt et al. 2020 (2020AJ....160..153B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BURT_ET_AL__2020): inclination 83.65 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Kokori et al. 2023 (2023ApJS..265....4K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KOKORI_ET_AL__2023): transit mid-time 2458983.66859 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 3 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
